clue.text: High-society tippler without allure

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the drinker's word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a toper is a habitual drinker
draw means attraction or appeal

explanation.surface: A society drinker who has lost all charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'High-society' as a hyphenated adjective is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for the highest social class or quality.

clue.text: Reflective article about writer's material

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for an object goes round the writer's stuff

parts.note: an article is a thing, an object
ink is what a writer uses

explanation.surface: A thoughtful essay about what an author writes with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a grammar word (A, AN, THE) but means an object, THING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reflective is pondering, in the act of using the mind.

clue.text: Musician filled with energy in the theatre

indicators.note: filled with means the performer's word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a player is someone who plays an instrument
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A lively musician performing on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre patron is a person found in the audience at a show; the definition describes where such a person is.

clue.text: Got one's reward when the nappy turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: diaper is the American word for a nappy

explanation.surface: A parent was paid back when the baby's nappy was flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPPY is British for a baby's diaper; 'turned up' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be repaid is to be compensated, rewarded for what one gave.

clue.text: Decline to be in Her Majesty's company

parts.note: in someone's company means with them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Refusing an invitation to spend time with the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to shrivel and fade, to go into decline.

clue.text: No tears if the accommodation is gratis

explanation.surface: Promising a tenant cheerfully that free lodging means no crying.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the answer as 'free of rents', a rent being a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent-free means without payment for lodging, and read cryptically means without rips or tears.

clue.text: A doctor cut mother in half-the snake!

indicators.note: cut together with in half shows the mother's word being split to take something inside
the mother's word is split into two halves with the doctor slotted between them

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic slices a mother in two, then a snake appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut ... in half' looks like surgery on mother; it splits the mother word so 'A doctor' can sit between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mamba is a venomous African serpent.

clue.text: A song by Albert in support of cross-dressing

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, so Albert's short form goes below the rest

parts.note: cross means angry, mad
rig is an outfit, a way of dressing
Al is short for Albert

explanation.surface: Albert sings while backing cross-dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross-dressing' looks like one idea but splits into two words; 'by' is a link, and 'in support of' places Albert's piece beneath the rest in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several voices.

clue.text: Underling delivers food around Islington

indicators.note: around shows the word for a repast enclosing the other piece

parts.note: a meal is a serving of food
N1 is the London postcode of Islington, written here as NI

explanation.surface: A servant delivering meals around a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a district of north London whose postcode is N1, read as NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial is a lowly servant doing humble work.

clue.text: State bringing woe to the spirit

parts.note: alas is a cry of woe
the ka is the spiritual double in ancient Egyptian belief

explanation.surface: A region of the country brings sorrow to the soul.
explanation.walkthrough: KA, the soul in Egyptian religion, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Having trouble appearing at a nightclub

explanation.surface: A performer struggling during a gig at a club.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in difficulty is to be stuck in a tight situation; a spot is also a nightclub, so performing there puts you at one.

clue.text: Casual query about a pop record's chances?

definitions.text: query about a pop record's chances?

explanation.surface: Someone casually asks whether a new single will chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard work is done carelessly; asking whether a single will be a chart success or a flop puts the same words as a question.

clue.text: Appropriate way to deal with a queue of customers

definitions.text: way to deal with a queue of customers

explanation.surface: The proper method for serving a line of shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fitting is acceptable or proper; customers queuing are served one after another in sequence.

clue.text: Knock back best-quality beer with all the trappings

indicators.note: knock back plays on drinking but here means the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as AI
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Downing top beer at a lavish formal do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' suggests drinking the beer; it actually reverses A1 LAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are ceremonial emblems and finery, the full trappings of office.

clue.text: Don a dhoti and get down to business

explanation.surface: Wrapping on a loincloth before getting to work.
explanation.walkthrough: A dhoti is a loincloth worn by men in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical idiom means preparing for action, literally tucking up a robe around one's middle, which a loincloth wearer does.

clue.text: Blow! The shoe leather has been slashed

parts.note: the upper is the leather top part of a shoe
cut means slashed

explanation.surface: A cobbler's dismay at finding the shoe leather gashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow!' looks like an exclamation of annoyance but defines a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is an upward punch in boxing, a kind of blow.

clue.text: Quaint description of anywhere but America

explanation.surface: A charming way to describe everywhere outside the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-world means charmingly old-fashioned; it also names Europe, Asia and Africa as opposed to the New World.

clue.text: A stain we removed with much anxiety

indicators.note: removed read as re-moved, moved again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fretfully trying to get rid of a mark on clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is read as re-moved: A STAIN WE moved again.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a nervous state means being agitated, perspiring with worry.

clue.text: To visit a capital is divine

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
caput means head, and capital also means the top of a column

explanation.surface: Touring a capital city is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective meaning heavenly but is the verb, to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to foretell, to look into the future.

clue.text: Rex came in slightly drenched-quite obviously!

indicators.note: came in shows the king's letter entering the other piece

parts.note: dipped means briefly immersed
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The king arrived a little wet, plainly so.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into DIPPED; a briefly dipped person would visibly drip.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dripped showed its wetness openly, the plain sign of being soaked.

clue.text: Scheme originating from French deputy

parts.note: de is French for from
vice- means deputy, as in vice-president

explanation.surface: A plot hatched by a French politician's second-in-command.
explanation.definitionFit: A device is a plan or trick contrived for a purpose.

clue.text: Where the barrister pleads as a precaution

explanation.surface: A lawyer argues a matter just to be safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister argues within a court action; a precaution is taken against a possibility.

clue.text: Calm at being put into position

indicators.note: being put into shows the small word going inside the other piece

parts.note: a place is a position

explanation.surface: Feeling settled at being given a role.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate is to pacify, soothing someone's anger.

clue.text: Refuse to get Dad's drink

parts.note: PA is Dad, with the possessive S
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Declining to fetch father a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline an offer is to let it go by, turning it down.

clue.text: What a beautiful fellow a fellow is!

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: An exclamation admiring a handsome man.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'fellow' changes sense: a don is a college fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Adonis was a youth of great looks, so the name means a handsome man.

clue.text: Filled the place of another to be in charge of divers round about

indicators.note: round about shows the word for assorted wrapping around the other piece

parts.note: divers, an old word, means several or various
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone stands in to supervise a team of underwater swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' looks like swimmers but is the old adjective meaning various.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious means done or felt as a substitute, standing in for someone else.

clue.text: From then on biblical studies were not affected

parts.note: since means from that time onwards
RE is Religious Education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Ever after, Bible study was left unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone genuine is unpretending, free of affectation.

clue.text: Put up before going to Connecticut

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut

explanation.surface: Building something before travelling to Connecticut.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect is to build or raise, setting a structure upright.

clue.text: Put down how assorted poets died

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An account of how a group of poets met their end.
explanation.definitionFit: Deposited means laid or set down somewhere.
